result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.line_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the line graph of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11664-L11821){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.line_graph(create_using_directed=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Line graph](/assets/graphs/algo-line-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a four-node star: a central hub H connected to three spokes A, B, C by edges labeled e1, e2, and e3. On the right, the corresponding line graph: each original edge becomes a node (labeled e1, e2, e3), and every pair of original edges shared the hub H, so the three new nodes form a triangle, drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} The line graph `L(G)` of a graph `G` transforms edges into nodes: each edge in `G` becomes a node in `L(G)`, and two nodes in `L(G)` are connected if and only if their corresponding edges in `G` share an endpoint. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [create_using_directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the resulting line graph should be directed. - If `None` (default): inherits directedness from source graph - If `True`: creates a directed line graph - If `False`: creates an undirected line graph For directed graphs, edge `(u,v)` connects to edge `(v,w)` if they share the intermediate node `v` (i.e., head of first = tail of second). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph representing the line graph. Each node in the line graph corresponds to an edge in the original graph, with attributes: - `source`: source node label of the original edge - `target`: target node label of the original edge - `edge_id`: ID of the original edge - `weight`: weight of the original edge (if weighted) ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For a graph $G = (V, E)$, the line graph $L(G)$ has one node for each edge of $G$, with two nodes in $L(G)$ adjacent whenever the corresponding edges of $G$ share an endpoint. On directed graphs the sharing must respect direction: edge $(u, v)$ links to $(v, w)$ but not to $(w, v)$. From that definition follow several handy identities. $|V(L(G))| = |E(G)|$ by construction, and for undirected $G$ the edge count is $|E(L(G))| = \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_v \deg(v)^2 - |E(G)|$. The line graph of $K_n$ is the triangular graph $T(n)$; the line graph of an $n$-cycle is another $n$-cycle; and the line graph of a star $K_{1,n}$ is the complete graph $K_n$, because all $n$ spokes share the hub. Whitney's theorem (1932) makes the whole construction robust: except for the degenerate case of $K_3$ vs $K_{1,3}$, $L(G) \cong L(H)$ implies $G \cong H$. That property is what makes line graphs useful for edge clustering, edge-community analysis, and modeling transfer points in transportation networks. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Line graph of a simple path: ::: {#9faf6f2e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create path: A -- B -- C g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 2 (one per edge) lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#73d20399 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 1 (edges A-B and B-C share B) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a triangle: ::: {#b823eaaa .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Triangle: A -- B -- C -- A g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") g.add_edge("C", "A") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 3 lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#f1e42b8a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 3 (also a triangle) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a directed graph: ::: {#285bb39b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Chain: A -> B -> C g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 2 lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#bde08003 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 1 (A->B connects to B->C) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Accessing original edge information: ::: {#7862ace7 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="X") g.add_node(label="Y") g.add_node(label="Z") g.add_edge("X", "Y", weight=2.0) g.add_edge("Y", "Z", weight=3.0) lg = g.line_graph() [lg.get_node(nid).attributes for nid in lg.get_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` [{'original_edge_id': 2, 'original_source': 2, 'original_target': 3, 'original_weight': 3.0}, {'original_edge_id': 1, 'original_source': 1, 'original_target': 2, 'original_weight': 2.0}] ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a star graph: ::: {#268d666a .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Star with center C g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="C") for i in range(4): g.add_node(label=f"L{i}") g.add_edge("C", f"L{i}") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 4 (one per spoke) lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#bb8fce7f .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 6 (all spokes share center - line graph of a star is a complete graph!) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
